request: Investigate the failing uart_tx test in regression and reproduce the failure.
expected_behavior: A root-cause analysis that names the defect in the uart_tx RTL under investigation and its outcome class, and a reproducing testbench that fails on that RTL under simulator.run with expect=fail and passes on the fixed RTL. The defect: the transmitter copies data into its hold register on every start pulse, including while a frame is in flight, although a start pulse while busy must be ignored; a second start with a different byte therefore replaces every bit of the frame in flight that has not gone out yet, and the first frame carries the second byte. The outcome is an RTL bug. The repro sends one byte, pulses start with a different byte during a later bit, reads the frame back at the middle of every bit, and fails on a wrong data bit, not on a build error or a missing verdict.
constraints: Work from the RTL under investigation, the failing log and the triage report; name the root cause in the RTL, not only the symptom in the log.

Write the repro as a self-checking testbench that ends with the verdict line the simulation gate reads, and that checks the behaviour the RTL's header states (a start pulse while busy is ignored), not the buggy RTL's output, and that does not depend on the names inside one implementation.
Choose the outcome class from rtl_bug, testbench_bug, infrastructure and spec_ambiguity, and say why the other three do not fit.
known_failure_modes: A root cause that names the symptom (the first frame carried the wrong byte) or a signal that is not the defect (the bit counter, the baud divider, the receiver model).
A repro that passes on the RTL under investigation, for example one that sends a second start only after busy falls; the repro gate refuses it before review.
A repro that fails on the RTL under investigation for another reason (a build error, a hang, a timing assumption), which the gate does not count as a reproduction.
A repro tied to one structure of the RTL (the name of the hold register), so it fails nothing on a second implementation with the same defect; the second control fails it.
A repro that fails the fixed RTL too, because it expects a second frame to be queued or checks the wrong bit time; the must-fail control fails it.

held_out.name: The seat's repro passes the fixed uart_tx and fails the RTL under investigation and its shift-register variant
The same repro passes a second, independent fixed implementation and fails both defective ones
